translations.text: Lo! We have heard heroes tell, men bold in deeds declare, what happened in the days of Maximian, who throughout the world, a wicked king,

…stirred up persecution, killed Christian men and threw down churches. The heathen war-leader poured out on the grassy plain the blood of those who praised God, the blood of the holy, of those who did what was right.
His kingdom was broad, wide and glorious over the nations of men, reaching over almost all the vast earth.
Mighty thanes went through the cities, as he had commanded. Often they stirred up violence, led astray in their deeds, those who hated the Lord's law through wicked craft.
They stirred up hostility, set up heathen idols, killed the holy, broke the learned, burned the chosen, and tormented God's warriors with spear and flame.

There was a certain man, rich in possessions and of noble family, a powerful reeve. He ruled fortified cities and guarded his homeland. He lived most of the time in the city of Nicomedia and kept a treasure-hoard there.
Often, against the word of God, he sought out heathen idols and shrines, very frequently and eagerly. His name was Heliseus; he held great and famous authority.
Then his heart began to love a maiden, Juliana (desire overcame him). She held holy faith in her spirit, and she was firmly resolved to keep her virginity pure of every sin for the love of Christ.
Then the maiden was betrothed to the wealthy man by her father's will. He did not fully know how things would turn out, or how she, young in spirit, scorned that union.
The fear of God was greater in her mind than all the treasure that lay among that nobleman's possessions.
Then the rich man, the man wealthy in gold, was eager in mind for the marriage, that the maiden should be made ready for him as quickly as possible, a bride for his home.
She firmly rejected that man's love, even though he owned riches under the lock of his hoard and countless ornaments on earth.
She scorned all of it, and spoke these words in front of the crowd of men: "I can tell you that you need not trouble yourself any further.
If you love and believe in the true God, raise up his praise, and acknowledge the protector of souls, I will be ready at once, without wavering, to do your will.
But I also tell you this: if by your deeds you commit yourself to a lesser god through devil-worship and call on a heathen idol, you cannot have me, and you cannot force me to be your wife.
You will never prepare pain so severe, through the violent hatred of harsh torments, that you could turn me away from these words."

When the nobleman, stained with wicked deeds, heard the maiden's words, he became swollen with anger. Fierce and blind of mind, he ordered swift messengers to fetch the holy maiden's father quickly for counsel.
Voices rose up after they leaned their spears together, those warriors. Both of them were heathen and sick with sins, the father-in-law and the son-in-law.
Then the guardian of the realm, the spear-bearer, spoke with a fierce heart to the maiden's father: "Your daughter has shown me dishonour.
She tells me outright that she cares nothing for my love as a kinsman or for my friendship. In my heart those insults are the greatest pain: that she rebuked me so angrily in front of this people,
and ordered me to worship a foreign god with riches, above the others we knew before, to praise him in words and honour him in my mind, or else not have her."
Then the stern-minded father-in-law grew dark in mood at those words, the maiden's father, and unlocked his heart:
"I swear this by the true gods, as I hope ever to find favour with them, or your goodwill from you, prince, in the wine-cities,
that if these words you tell me are true, dearest of men, I will not spare her, but will give her up to destruction, glorious prince, into your power."
Condemn her to death if that seems fitting to you, or let her live, whichever you prefer."
Then he went boldly to speak with the maiden, resolute and angrily perverse, swollen with rage, to where he knew the young woman, glad of heart, kept her dwelling.
Then he spoke these words: "You are my daughter, the dearest and sweetest in my heart, my only one on earth, the light of my eyes, Juliana!
In your folly, through your defiance, you have taken up a useless course, against the judgement of the wise.
You reject your bridegroom too strongly, of your own will. He is better than you, nobler on earth, richer in treasures of wealth. He is good to have as a friend.
So it is right that you do not reject the love of this man, a lasting and happy love."
Then the blessed Juliana gave him an answer (she had firmly established her friendship with God):

"I will never agree to be joined in kinship with this prince unless he worships the God of hosts more eagerly than he has so far, and loves with offerings the one who created light, heaven and earth and the expanse of the seas, and the whole circle of the world's dwellings.
He cannot otherwise bring me to his dwelling. He must seek bridal love from another woman, with his possessions; he has none here."
Then in anger the father gave her a hostile answer; not at all did he [?] adornments:
"I will bring it about, if my life lasts, if you do not first give up your folly, and you go on worshipping strange gods and abandon those that are dearer to us,
which stand for the good of this people, that you will soon forfeit your life and die by the grip of wild beasts, if you will not consent to the agreement, the union with the noble man.
Great and presumptuous for one such as you is this undertaking, that you scorn our lord."
Then the blessed one, wise and dear to God, Juliana, gave him answer: "I will tell you the truth; as long as I live I will not tell a lie.

Never do I fear your judgments, nor do the terrors of punishment trouble me, the horrors of war that you, evildoer, violently threaten me with. Nor will you ever, through your error, manage to turn me from the praise of Christ."
Then the father was furious with his daughter, angry and fierce, savage and cruel of spirit.

He then ordered her to be scourged, tormented with pain, afflicted with punishments, and spoke these words: "Change your mind, and take back the words you foolishly spoke before, when you scorned the worship of our gods."

The fearless one, Juliana, gave him an answer from her spirit's thought: "Never will you teach me to promise tribute to falsehoods, to dumb and deaf idols, to the enemies of souls, the worst servants of torment,
but I honour the Lord of glory, of the world and of majesty, and I trust in him alone for everything, that he may be my protector, helper and saviour against the fiends of hell."

Then in anger Africanus, the maiden's father, gave her into the power of enemies, to Eleusius. At daybreak, after the coming of light, he ordered her to be led to his judgment seat. The nobles marvelled at the maiden's beauty, all the people together.
Then the nobleman, her bridegroom, first greeted her with gentle words: "My sweetest radiance of the sun, Juliana! Lo, you have splendour, ample gifts, the bloom of youth!

If you will yet please our gods, and seek protection for yourself with such gracious ones, favour with the holy ones, then a countless number of cruelly devised tortures and grim afflictions that are prepared for you will be turned away from you; but they await you if you will not sacrifice to the true gods."
The noble maiden gave him an answer: "Never will you compel me with your threats, nor prepare so many cruel tortures, that I will love your fellowship,

unless you abandon those falsehoods, the worship of idols, and wisely acknowledge the God of glory, the Creator of souls, the Ruler of mankind, in whose power all created things are forever, without end."

Then before the people the ruler of the people, fierce in mind, spoke threatening words and grew very angry. Out of malicious vengeance he ordered the sinless maiden to be stretched out naked and beaten with whips.
Then the warrior laughed and spoke mocking words: "This is mastery in our contest seized right at the start!
Still I will grant you your life, though you have spoken many reckless words before, and denied too strongly that you would love the true gods.

Since you oppose them, the reward that awaits you afterwards will be the terrors of punishment, unless you first make peace with them, and after your sinful words offer them acceptable sacrifice and settle peace."

Let the strife rest, this hateful quarrel among the people. If after this you go on following error through your foolish will, then I shall of necessity, driven by hostility, avenge in the grimmest way the offence against the gods,
the angry slander that you have begun to utter with blasphemies against the best and the mildest of those that men know, whom this people has long worshipped among them."
The noble spirit answered him unafraid: "I do not fear your judgments, accursed criminal, nor the evil of your torments.
I have as my hope the Guardian of the heavenly kingdom, the gentle protector, the Ruler of hosts, who will shield me against your sorcery, from the grip of the hostile ones whom you count as gods.
They are lacking in every good: empty, useless, unprofitable. No man will find any benefit there, or true peace, though he seeks friendship from them.
He will find no help there among devils. I fix my mind on the Lord, who rules forever over every power, the Possessor of glory and of every victory. He is the true King."
Then it seemed shameful to the leader of the people that he could not change the mind, the purpose, of the maiden.

He ordered her to be hung by the hair and raised up on a high beam, where the sun-bright one suffered blows, ceaseless persecution, for six hours of the day. Then the hateful foe immediately ordered her to be taken down again, and commanded that she be led to prison.
The praise of Christ was firmly bound in her heart, her gentle mind, her unbroken strength.
Then the prison door, the work of hammers, was shut with a lock. The holy one, steadfast in faith, remained inside.
Always in her heart she praised the King of glory, the God of the heavenly kingdom, the Saviour of men, in that prison cell, covered in darkness.
The Holy Spirit was her constant companion. Then suddenly there came into that prison-house the enemy of men, skilled in evil.

He had the form of an angel, the enemy of souls, skilled in causing grief, the captive of hell. He spoke to the holy woman: "What are you suffering, you who are the dearest and most honoured to the King of glory, our Lord?
This judge has prepared the worst torments for you, endless pain, if you will not offer sacrifice, wise-minded one, and please his gods.
Be quick, when he orders you to be led out from here, to offer sacrifice promptly, a victory offering, before death takes you, death in front of the company of men.
In that way, blessed maiden, you shall escape the judge's anger."
Then she, who was not afraid and who was pleasing to Christ, boldly asked where he had come from.
The outcast answered her: "I am an angel of God, come down from above, an excellent thegn, and I have been sent to you, holy, from on high.
Hard and wondrously cruel torments have been prepared for you as a deadly punishment. God, the Son of the Ruler, has commanded that you be told to protect [?] yourself from them."
Then the maiden was struck with terror at the sudden message that the monster, the adversary of glory, spoke to her.
Then the young woman, without guile, began to steady her mind firmly and to call on God: "Now I will ask you, protector of men, eternal Almighty, by the noble creation which you,
Father of angels, established in the beginning, that you not let me turn away from praising your blessed gift, as this messenger who stands before me announces to me a perilous, sudden message.
So I will ask you, merciful one, glory of kings, guardian of majesty, to make known to me what this thegn is, flying through the air, who urges me away from you onto a hard road."

A beautiful voice answered her from the clouds, uttering words: "Seize that insolent one and hold him fast until he tells his errand truthfully, all of it from the beginning, and what his origins are."
Then the maiden's spirit was gladdened, she who was glorious in her judgment. She seized that devil [?] "to deliver the King of all kings to death.
Further, I contrived that the soldier began to wound the Ruler, in the sight of the multitude, so that blood and water both together poured down to the earth.
Again, I put it into Herod's mind to order John beheaded, when the holy man rebuked him with words for his love of the woman, an unlawful marriage.
I also taught Simon, with cunning thoughts, to start a quarrel with the chosen thegns of Christ, and to attack the holy men with scorn through deep heresy, saying they were sorcerers.

I ventured with crafty tricks when I deceived Nero, so that he ordered Christ's thegns, Peter and Paul, to be killed. Before that, Pilate hanged the Ruler of the heavens, the mighty Lord, on the cross at my instigation.
Likewise I also taught Aegeas, so that in his folly he ordered holy Andrew to be hanged on a high tree, so that he sent forth his spirit from the gallows into the splendour of glory.
Thus I, with my brothers, have committed many cruel evils, dark sins, which I cannot tell or recount in full, nor know the number of those harsh, hostile thoughts."
The holy Juliana answered him through the gift of the Spirit: "You must go further still, enemy of mankind, in telling your errand, and say who sent you to me."
The monster gave her an answer, seized with fear, despairing of peace:
"Listen! My father, king of the inhabitants of hell, sent me here to you on this journey from that narrow home. In that hall of sorrow he is more eager than I am for every kind of evil.
When he sends us to turn the mind of the righteous through deception and to turn them away from salvation, we are sad of mind and afraid in spirit.
Our lord, that terrible prince, is not gentle with us if we have done no evil; after that we dare not go anywhere into his presence.

Then he sends thegns out of the darkness throughout the wide earth and orders them to stir up violence: if we are met on the earth's paths, or found far or near, they are to bind us and scourge us with torments in the surging fire.
If, despite hindrance, the mind of the righteous, the thought of the holy, does not turn away, we suffer the hardest and worst torments through painful blows.
Now you can see the truth in your own mind: I was forced by necessity into this venture, oppressed time and again, so that I came to you."
Then again the holy woman began to question in words the enemy of men, the worker of strife, the originator of ancient sins:

"You must tell me more, enemy of souls: how, wrapped in deceit, you do the greatest harm to the righteous through the slippery path of sins." The fiend, the faithless outcast, answered her and spoke these words:

"Blessed maiden, I will make known to you, from beginning to end, every one of the evils I have committed, and not just a few times, with the wounds of sin, so that you yourself may see the more clearly that this is true and not false.
With bold thought I believed and was sure that I could turn you away from salvation easily, by my skill alone,

so that you would renounce the King of heaven, the Lord of victories, turn to a lesser one, and sacrifice to the author of sins. In this way I turn the minds of the righteous through many different guises.
When I find a man setting his spirit firmly on God's will, I am ready at once to bring against him many lusts of the mind, grim thoughts and secret errors, through a host of delusions.
I make the pleasures of sin sweet to him, and wicked desires of the heart, so that he soon gives himself to vice and obeys my teachings.
I inflame him with sins so strongly that, burning, he leaves off his prayer and strides off forcefully. Because he loves his vices, he cannot stay steadfast any longer in the place of prayer.

So I bring terror and hatred to the one whose life I begrudge, and his faith in the light. If he is willing, in the desire of his mind, to obey my teachings and commit sin, then afterward he must go away stripped of good virtues.

If I meet a brave and courageous champion of the Lord standing against the storm of arrows, one who will not flee far from the battle but, wise of mind, raises his shield against me, the holy shield, the spiritual war-gear,
he will not betray God, but, bold in prayer, he holds his ground firmly on foot. Then I must turn away far from there, humiliated, robbed of joys, into the grip of the flames, to lament my grief,

so that I cannot advance into the fight by force of strength, then I must sadly look for another in the bannered troop, a less courageous and slacker warrior, whom I can stir up with my leaven and hold back from the battle.

Even if he begins some spiritual good work for God, I am ready at once to search through all his inner thoughts, to see how firmly his mind is fastened within and what defence has been built. I open the gate of that wall by doing harm.

the tower is pierced and the entrance opened when I first send bitter thoughts into him, into his heart, through a flight of arrows, through the various desires of the mind, so that it seems better to him to commit sins, the lusts of the body, than to praise God.
I am an eager teacher, so that he lives by my customs, plainly turned away from Christ's law, his mind corrupted and under my power in the pit of sins.
I care much more eagerly about the soul and the ruin of the spirit than about the body, which must lie in the grave in this world, a comfort to the worm, buried in the earth."
Then the maiden spoke again: "Tell me, wretched creature, unclean spirit, ruler of darkness: how did you push your way in among the pure?
Long ago you faithlessly fought against Christ, made war, and plotted against the saints. The pit of hell was dug deep for you, and there, driven by need, you went to live because of your pride."
"I thought that you would have to be all the warier of such an encounter with the righteous, and all the less bold, since he has often withstood you, through the King of glory, against your will."

Then the accursed one, the wretched monster, answered her: "First you tell me how you became so daring through deep thought, so bold in battle beyond all womankind, that you bound me so fast in fetters, completely defenceless.
you have placed your trust in the eternal God, who sits in majesty, the Lord of mankind, just as I fix my hope on my father, the king of the dwellers in hell.

When I am sent against the righteous to turn their minds to wicked deeds and their hearts away from salvation, sometimes my will and my hope are denied among the holy, because they resist me, just as sorrow befell me here on my journey.
I learned that myself far too late. Now, guilty, I must suffer shame for a long time after this.
So I beg you by the power of the Highest and by the grace of the King of heaven, the Lord of glory, who suffered on the tree of the cross: have mercy on me in my need,
so that I, unhappy one, may not perish entirely, even though I came to you so daringly and so recklessly, where I had never before expected such a time of trial for myself."
Then the radiantly beautiful candle of glory spoke these words to the traitor:
"You must confess more of your evil deeds, wretched spirit of hell, before you may go from here: what great wicked deeds you have carried out to harm the race of men with dark delusions."
The devil answered her: "Now I hear from your words that I must, of necessity and forced by afflictions, reveal my mind as you command me, and endure harsh compulsion.
"This is a very hard time, an immense affliction. I must suffer and endure everything at your judgment, and reveal the wicked deeds, dark ones, that I have plotted far and wide.

Often I took away sight. With evil thoughts I blinded countless men of the human race. With a helmet of mist, through the point of poison and with dark showers, I covered the light of their eyes. With wicked snares I broke the feet of some. Some I sent into burning, into the enclosure of flame, so that their footprints were seen for the last time.
I also made it happen to some that their bodies spewed blood, so that they suddenly lost their lives through the surging of their veins.

Through my skills, some on a sea-voyage were sunk in the waters on the waves, in the sea-flood, beneath the fierce current. Some I committed to the cross, so that they gave up their lives in their blood on the high gallows.
Some I drew on with my teachings and urged to strife, so that, drunk with beer, they suddenly renewed old grudges.
I poured them strife from the cup, so that in the wine-hall, through the grip of the sword, they let their doomed souls hurry out of the body, afflicted with pains.
Some whom I found without the sign of God, careless and unblessed, I boldly killed with my own hands through various deaths, by cunning devices.

Even if I sat here a long summer's day, I could not tell all the hardships that I have brought about in wickedness, early and late, ever since the heavens were first raised up, and the course of the stars,
and the earth made firm, and the first humans, Adam and Eve. I took life from them, and I taught them to give up the love of the Lord, the eternal blessed gift,

and the bright wealth of their dwelling. As a result, misery came upon them both for life, and likewise upon their offspring, the darkest of evil deeds. Why should I count up any more of this endless evil?
I brought about all the cruel strifes throughout the nations of men that have arisen for the human race, for men on earth, through all ages since the beginning of the world.
None of them, holy one, ever dared to touch me with their hands as boldly as you have now. No man on earth was so bold through holy might, none of the patriarchs or the prophets.
Though the God of hosts, the King of glory, revealed to them the spirit of wisdom, a grace beyond measure, I was still allowed to reach them.
None of them so boldly laid bonds on me or crushed me with afflictions before you did now. You have overpowered and firmly seized that great might of mine

which my father gave me, the enemy of mankind, the prince out of darkness, when he ordered me to set out so that I should make sin sweet to you. There sorrow came upon me, a heavy hand-to-hand struggle.
After this painful punishment I will have no reason to laugh about this journey among my kinsmen, when I, full of grief, must give my account of service in that grim home."
Then the reeve, a man with a gallows-minded heart, ordered Juliana, holy in spirit, to be led out of the narrow building to his judgment seat to speak with the heathens.
Inspired in her breast, the holy one dragged the heathen devil along, fast in bonds. Then, in sorrow, he began to lament his journey, bewail his pain and mourn his fate. He spoke these words:
"I beg you, my lady Juliana, for the sake of God's peace, do not bring further shame on me, and disgrace before men, beyond what you did earlier,

when you overpowered the wisest one, the king of the dwellers in hell, under the shadow of the prison in the city of fiends. He is our father, the wicked lord of murder. Lo, you have chastised me with painful blows!
I know for a truth that never, early or late, have I met any woman like you in the world, any of the race of maidens bolder in thought or more unyielding.

It is clear from me that you have become shameless in every respect and wise in spirit." Then, after a time of torment, the maiden let him go, the adversary of souls, to seek out the darkness in the black abyss, in the ruin of torments.
So he, the proclaimer of evil, knew all the better how to tell his kinsmen, the thanes of torment, how things had gone for him on his journey.
[?] eagerly praised before on high, and his holy word, and they said truly that he alone ruled over every victory, over all creation, and over eternal blessed gifts."

Then an angel of God came, shining in splendour, and thrust the fire aside. He freed and protected her, pure of guilt and without sin, and scattered the fiercely greedy flame. The holy one, the chief of maidens, stood unharmed in the middle.
…so that it was a grief for the rich man to endure, if he could have changed it in the world. Stained with sins, he sought how he might find for her the most painful death through the worst torments.
The fiend was not slow. He taught him to order an earthen vessel to be made with wondrous skill, amid the din of war, and to surround it with tree-trunks and wood.

Then the hard man ordered the clay vessel to be filled with lead, and then commanded the greatest of pyre-fires to be kindled, a pyre lit, which was surrounded on every side with burning brands. The bath boiled hot.

Then, swollen with anger, he quickly ordered the woman free of sins to be shoved into the boiling lead, though she was without guilt. Then the vessel was split apart and the flame let loose. The lead sprang out far and wide, hot and greedy for slaughter.
The men were terrified and struck with fear by that rush. Seventy-five of the heathen host were burned up there by the fire's blast. Yet the holy woman still stood with her beauty unharmed.

Neither her fringe nor her garment, nor her hair nor her skin, nor her body nor her limbs were marked by the fire. She stood in the flame wholly unharmed and gave thanks for everything to the Lord of lords.

Then the judge grew fierce and savage-minded and began to tear his garment. He also bared his teeth and gnashed them, raged in his mind like a wild beast, roared in his gallows-minded rage, and blamed his gods because their might could not withstand the woman's will.
The glorious maiden was resolute and unafraid, mindful of the strength and the will of the Lord.

Then the judge, troubled with sorrow, ordered that the holy-minded woman be put to death by the bite of the sword, deprived of her head, she who was chosen by Christ. The killing did him no good once he came to know more of its outcome.

Then the holy woman's hope was renewed and the maiden's mind was greatly gladdened, when she heard the men devise their malicious counsel that her end must come, out of the days of strife, and her life be released.
Then he who was full of crimes ordered the pure and chosen woman, free of sins, to be led to her death.

Then suddenly the abject spirit of hell came, wretched and miserable, singing a song of harm. He was the accursed one whom she had earlier bound and beaten with torments. Full of sorrowful songs, he cried out before the crowd:
"Now pay her back with grief because she despised the power of our gods and humiliated me most of all, so that I became an informer against myself.
Let her receive a hateful reward through the weapon's track. Avenge the old enmity and the wrong done to me.

I remember that sorrow, how in a single night, held fast in bonds, I suffered countless troubles and hardships, an immense evil." Then the blessed Juliana looked toward the hostile one. She heard the devil of hell lamenting his harm.
Then the enemy of mankind began to hasten away in flight, seeking the torments, and spoke these words: "Woe is me, ruined one!
"Now it is very likely that she will humiliate wretched me again with evil miseries, as she did to me before."
Then she was led near the boundary of the land, to the place where the stern-minded men meant to kill her with battle-hatred.

Then she began to teach the people and to urge them from their crimes toward praise. She promised them comfort and the way to glory, and spoke these words: "Remember the joy of warriors and the majesty of glory, the hope of the holy, the God of heaven's angels.
He is worthy to be praised by the nations of men and by the whole race of angels up in the heavens. He is the high power, with whom help is found, eternal forever, for those who are to have it.
Therefore, dear company, as one who keeps the law, I wish to teach you to make your house firm, so that the winds may not throw it down with sudden blasts.
The wall must stand the firmer and strong against the showers of storms, the thoughts of sin.

With the love of peace and with bright faith, firm of heart, fasten your foundation to the living stone. Keep true faith and peace among yourselves in your hearts, and the holy mysteries with the intention of your minds.

Then the Father almighty will grant you mercy, and with the God of powers you will have comfort in the greatest need, after your sorrows. For you yourselves do not know when you will depart from here, the end of your lives.
It seems prudent to me that you stay watchful and keep guard against the battle-noise of the enemies, so that the adversaries do not bar your way to the city of glory.
Pray to the Son of God that the Lord of angels, the Ruler of mankind, the Giver of victories, may be merciful to me.
Peace be with you, and true love always." Then by the stroke of a sword her soul was led out of her body to the long joy.
Then Eleusius, the sinful destroyer, terrified, went to his ship with a band of men and sought the sea. He was tossed over the waters for a long while on the swans' road.
The flood carried them all off, the band of men and himself with them, before they had sailed to land, through a fierce onslaught.
There [thirty] and four more besides of the race of warriors were deprived of life through the surge of the wave. Abased along with their lord, stripped of comforts, without hope, they went to hell.

The thanes in that dark home, the band of retainers in that deep pit, had no need to expect appointed treasures from their leader, or to think that in the wine-hall, over the beer-bench, they would receive rings and apple-shaped gold.
Very differently was the body of the holy woman carried with songs of praise by a great host to the earthen grave. The great multitude brought it inside the city.
There afterwards, as the years went by, the praise of God was raised with great majesty among the people, up to this day.
I have great need that the holy woman give me help when the dearest of all part from each other: when the wedded pair, the two companions, tear apart their kinship and their great heart's love.

My soul must leave the body on a journey to an unknown dwelling, and I myself do not know where. I must go from here to seek another place in keeping with my former works, to go according to my deeds of old.

Sorrowful, C (ᚳ), Y (ᚣ) and N (ᚾ) will depart. The King, the giver of victories, will be stern when E (ᛖ), W (ᚹ) and U (ᚢ), stained with sins, wait in terror for what he will judge for them according to their deeds, as the reward for their lives.
ᛚ ᚠ [runes L, F; meaning uncertain] tremble and linger, anxious with sorrow. I remember all the pain, the wounds of sins, that I committed in the world, later or earlier.
I must lament this tearfully, with tears. The time came too late for me to feel shame for my evil deeds, while spirit and body still travelled together, whole, on earth.
Then I will need mercy, so that the holy woman may intercede for me with the highest king. Need urges me to this, a great sorrow of mind.

I ask every man of the human race who recites this poem to remember me by my name, for I am in need, and to pray earnestly to the Lord that the protector of the heavens, the ruler of powers, give me help on that great day,

the Father, the Spirit of comfort, in that perilous hour, the judge of deeds, and the beloved Son, when the Trinity, sitting in majesty in unity, assigns to every member of the human race a reward according to his works throughout the bright creation.
Grant us, God of hosts, joy of princes, that we may find your face gracious at that glorious time. Amen.
